voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Yale University keeps a book, six hundred years old, that no one has ever been able to read.
It is written in an alphabet of its own. Twenty or so letters, page after page, that no one has matched to any known language.
It is full of drawings: plants nobody can name, circles like star charts, and pools of water linked by pipes.
The calfskin it is written on has been carbon dated to the early fourteen hundreds.
Wartime codebreakers tried. So have linguists, and computers. No reading has ever been proved.
